overview: This Senate resolution celebrates the 175th anniversary of the Young Men's Christian Association (YMCA) in the United States, which was founded in Boston in 1851. It highlights the YMCA's history, including inventing basketball, offering early night school and English classes, and starting the first group swim lessons, and its present role as a major provider of child care, youth programs, swim lessons and fitness programs in communities across the country. The Senate congratulates the YMCA, thanks its staff and volunteers, and encourages continued efforts to reduce social isolation and loneliness. It was approved on March 12, 2026.
for: Supporters say the resolution recognizes an organization that has served American communities for generations through youth programs, child care and health activities.
against: Critics say it is symbolic and doesn't change any law or spending.
